items.fact: Pitch count: 8 (pitches field / prose) vs 6 (approach text and pitch_detail rows)
items.prior_evidence: Depends on the STRUCTURAL item below. 8 pitches is the published count for the Southeast Ridge (the row's name, beta, rappels); the six pitch_detail rows and the '6 pitches' in partner_requirements and seasonal_hazards describe the col-side East Ridge. No second full description of the Southeast Ridge was found this pass (archived climber's log has only South Route and NE Couloir entries), so the breakdown cannot be rebuilt.

items.fact: Route name 'Southeast Ridge' vs prose describing the 'East Ridge' from the Argonaut-Colchuck col
items.prior_evidence: STRUCTURAL: the row fuses two routes. name, face, pitches (8), beta and rappels describe the Southeast Ridge (II 5.6, 8 pitches to the SE spire, two single or one double rappel into the notch), which two listings name as a separate route; pitch_detail (starts 'From the Argonaut-Colchuck col'), descent_text ('reversing the East Ridge ... notch just west of the lone gendarme'), rappel_detail (traverse toward the east gully) and the '6 pitches' text describe the East Ridge from the col, which has its own route page. What should change: either rename the row to the col-side East Ridge and move the Southeast Ridge facts (8 pitches, SE spire, notch rappels) to a separate row, or replace pitch_detail/descent_text/rappel_detail with a Southeast Ridge description once one can be read in full. Needs a rename or a rebuilt breakdown, which the patch format cannot express.

items.fact: Day-2 schedule spans 4:30 AM-9:00 PM (16.5 hrs) vs the day's stated 13 hours; timing.totalHrs 19; partner_requirements '10-hr round trip from bivy'; gain_ft 4300 vs itinerary total 4157

items.fact: Elevation gain to the crag
items.prior_evidence: Same as Drilling Me Softly: no published approach gain for the Silver Basin crags; ground heights give ~4,250 ft at the FS 9070 road end and ~4,670 ft at the crag, i.e. ~400 ft of net rise, which is only a floor for cumulative gain, so 750 is neither confirmed nor provably wrong. No patch.

items.fact: Season / when the access road is open
items.prior_evidence: Same as Drilling Me Softly: one source gives FR-9070 snow-free July to November, another June-October as the period the road is open; no third source states an opening month. No window adopted.

items.fact: Trailhead waypoint sits on the crag coordinate with the area's 4,585 ft elevation
items.prior_evidence: STRUCTURAL: waypoints[0] 'FS Road 9070 Turnaround at Silver Basin' carries the crag's own coordinate (47.36741,-121.45564, identical to waypoints[1]) and the parent area's 4,585 ft. The same defect on sibling Drilling Me Softly was fixed by moving the pin to the road end: the U.S. Forest Service road layer ends the left-fork spur at 47.37289,-121.45781 and OpenStreetMap's 9070-310 track at 47.37310,-121.45793 (two independent road datasets ~25 m apart); USGS ground there is ~4,254 ft. Move waypoints[0] to that point and set elev/elevFt 4254. A pin move is outside the patch format, and setting only the elevation would leave the pin on the crag, so no patch here.

items.fact: Commitment/technical grade disagrees across three fields (II vs I-II vs III)
items.prior_evidence: Third pass. Search again surfaces only the same split: one route database gives Grade III (matching alpine_grade), the long-standing route site gives Grade I-II on its Sitkum Glacier page (its peak page also calls the standard route Grade I, same site so counted once), and club, guide and trip-report pages give no Roman grade. The range rule needs two independent sources for each end; the III end has one, so no range is written and grade (II), commitment (I-II) and alpine_grade (III) stay as they are.

items.fact: Structured waypoints/road/approach_logistics describe a different trailhead than the approach/itinerary prose
items.prior_evidence: Third pass. Recent North Fork Sauk reports confirm White Pass at about 9 mi / 6,000 ft (5.5 mi of valley trail then ~3,000 ft of switchbacks) and one June 2026 party logged 13.9 mi and 6,324 ft to a camp on the Glacier Gap line, but none gives the PCT mileage from White Pass over Red Pass to the Sitkum Creek climbers' path or on to Boulder Basin. A February 2025 forum report exists for a winter White Chuck/Sitkum ascent (page blocked), so the old line is still used in winter on foot along the closed road. Rewriting itinerary days, timing and descent for the North Fork Sauk line would need computed segment distances, so no patch.

items.fact: total elevation gain
items.prior_evidence: Still real: gain_ft 4,799 / loss_ft 7,000 vs itinerary days of 7,200 up and down and a totalNote of 6,500-7,000 ft. items.fact: commitment grade: grade 'IV' vs commitment 'III' vs alpine_grade 'Grade III'
items.prior_evidence: Still real: grade 'IV' vs commitment 'III' and alpine_grade 'Grade III (historic...)'. Every graded listing found on the third pass (route database, club route pages, AAJ notes, trip reports) grades the Northeast Buttress (III-IV or IV, 5.4-5.5); none publishes a commitment grade for the direct Northeast Face climbed by Beckey and Parrott in 1954. Rule 2 cannot apply because no source grades this line at all.

items.fact: Whether a wilderness permit is needed
items.prior_evidence: Still present (permit and access.permit: free self-issue permit at the trailhead; waypoint 0 directions, itinerary.cal, access.overnight_permit and bivy[1]: no permit). The forest's wilderness-regulations page names the free self-issue permit requirement only for the Alpine Lakes Wilderness, and its Wild Sky page mentions only passes and general rules, which leans toward no permit; the peak's route page and the club route page say no parking pass is needed at the roadside start but say nothing about a wilderness permit. Both leaning statements come from one agency, and nothing states the Wild Sky rule outright, so no patch.

items.fact: access.closures is null while the bivy entries say the Rachel Lake trailhead / Box Canyon road were inside a 2026 wildfire closure
items.prior_evidence: The current Forest Service order (06-17-03-2026-44, effective 18 Sep 2026 through 31 Oct 2026) still lists Rachel Lake Trail 1313, Rachel Lake Trailhead and road 4930 as closed. But a news report updated 21-24 Sep 2026 says the Three Queens closure orders were lifted in parts of the Cle Elum Ranger District without naming which, so the two sources do not agree on the current state. A time-bound closure should be written from a confirmed current order; nothing is patched.

items.fact: gain_ft/loss_ft 5,700 vs the itinerary's day gains (4,800 + 1,900 + 900) and losses; dist_km 38.62 km (24 mi) vs ~13.5 mi one way / ~30 mi round trip
items.prior_evidence: Still real. New on this pass: a multi-day traverse report of the same Buck Creek Pass / High Pass / Louis Creek Basin line gives ~30 mi and 10,200 ft gained / 10,400 ft lost, but it exits by Little Giant Pass, so it is not this out-and-back; a 2025 High Pass report gives 8,150 ft / 23-27.5 mi for a different outing; the club route page's 20 mi / 6,000 ft is the Little Giant line. The USGS elevation service gives ~2,760 ft at the trailhead pin and ~8,449 ft at the summit pin, so 5,700 is not provably below the net rise. items.fact: Climbing season: May-Jun header vs a season description running through September
items.prior_evidence: Deep retry found two dated ascents of this White River / Thunder Creek southwest-face line, both in late spring: May 28-30, 1977 (rock scramble and snow climb, camp in Chalangin Basin) and June 1, 2025 (icy from an overnight freeze, crampons needed; that author waited for late May after April and November attempts failed). A November 2024 attempt on the same line turned back on wind slab 500 ft below the top, and its author describes an earlier late-October descent of the basin through open trees. These support late spring but do not state a window, and nothing found confirms or rules out a summer dry scramble (the only summer attempt, August 2023, failed on the overgrown trail), so neither season nor best_season/climate is changed.

items.fact: Commitment grade: IV vs III
items.prior_evidence: Third pass. The first-ascent party's own forum trip report (archived) names the route 'Holsten-Hilden 1,600 ft WI3 M6, steep snow' with no Roman numeral; the regional new-route register lists the January 2011 ascent without a grade; a list of forgotten Cascade alpine ice routes does not grade it. The only numerals remain IV (the AAJ first-ascent note) and III (the route listing), one source each, so neither numeral nor a III-IV range (needs two sources per end) can be adopted.

items.fact: trailhead-to-high-camp distance (dist_km 4 mi vs itinerary day 1 5.7 mi vs camp waypoint distMi 3.2)
items.prior_evidence: Third pass. A guide service states Eldorado Creek trailhead to the Eldorado/Inspiration high camp as 3 miles (5-7 h), which fits the camp waypoint's 3.2 mi; a trip-report blog's 'approach gains 6,300 ft over 5 miles' and the older snippet of ~6 mi to a camp at the Inspiration/McAllister saddle measure to farther points. Round trips also disagree: the club route page gives this route 12.0 mi and 7,000 ft, a Dorado Needle + Klawatti trip 15 mi, and the row itself carries ~16 mi (totalNote, 25.75 km in approach). The itinerary's day-1 camp is near the McAllister/Marble Creek col, farther than the waypoint's Inspiration-flats camp, so the figures describe different endpoints. No one-way distance to the row's camp or the route base is stated twice, and no two sources state the same round trip for rule 1, so no patch.

items.fact: Whether the approach goes via Prusik Pass (beta) or deliberately avoids it (approach / baseFinding)
items.prior_evidence: STRUCTURAL: the row holds two lines and cannot be made consistent without a rename. The most documented line in current use is Prusik Pass then west up the peak's eastern arm to the NE summit (the peak's long-standing route page: 'an easy scramble from Prusik Pass' heading west up the shoulder; a 2020s Enchantment-slam trip report: from Prusik Pass west up the eastern arm, one steep step near 7,900 ft, class 3/4 summit block) - this is what beta and pitch_detail rows 3-4 describe. A different scramble leaving the basin directly between Lakes Reginleif and Sigrun is documented by one trail blog (class 2-3 with class 3-4 exposed spots, summit not identified) and the peak page's separate class 4 south-side line to the SW summit - this is what name 'Southwest Scramble', face, overview, approach and the variant baseFinding describe, while they also say the route ends on the NE summit. No source ties the Reginleif/Sigrun line to the NE summit. Owner should either (a) rename the row to the Prusik Pass / east-arm line to the NE summit and rewrite face, overview's last sentence, the approach's Reginleif/Sigrun sentence and baseFinding's 'does not lead to this scramble' to match beta and pitch_detail, or (b) keep 'Southwest Scramble' as the south-side line to the SW summit (class 4) and rewrite beta, pitch_detail rows 3-6 and descent_text; option (a) follows the delegated rule.

No patch; the approach paragraph and the waypoint distances need a sourced North Fork Sauk mileage.

items.fact: Summit-day duration vs. its own timestamped schedule
items.prior_evidence: Third attempt. Searches of guide pages, club trip reports and the peak's climber log found only descriptions of the Northeast Face as several pitches of snow and ice to about 60 degrees, best in early fall, and summit-day times for the standard East Ridge (3-5 hours camp to summit; one party under 2 hours up and 1 down). No source gives times for the face itself, so the day's 9 hours and its 12-hour clock schedule cannot be reconciled without inventing times.

items.fact: which approach the trip plan uses, and the one-way distance
items.prior_evidence: STRUCTURAL: itinerary.days[0] (title, note, objective, and the ~9:00 AM, ~12:00 PM and 2:00 PM schedule items), itinerary.days[1] note and last schedule item ('retrace Day 1's ridge traverse'), itinerary.cal ('camping on Ragged Ridge'), itinerary.totalNote ('high camp on Ragged Ridge') and timing.sectionBreakdown[0].note all describe the Ragged Ridge crest traverse over Cub Peak, while every other field describes dropping from Easy Pass into Fisher Creek past Fisher Camp and climbing the south basin to a ~6,700 ft shoulder camp; the day-1 plan should be rewritten to the Fisher Creek line (one party on that line reached flat ground at the 6,700 ft rib step 4.2 hr from the car). Both lines are documented by one detailed report each (Fisher Creek line; crest over Cub Peak with a bivy west of Kitling), and a peak page describes a third, a traverse west below the ridge from just before Easy Pass without descending to Fisher Creek, so no source ranks one as standard and the rewrite would need schedule times no source states. dist_km (12.1) already matches the approach text's ~12 km one way, so the distance half of this item is settled on the live row.

items.fact: Which drainage/trail the approach to Rimrock Ridge uses
items.prior_evidence: STRUCTURAL: the approach's final leg ('follow the Agnes Creek Trail roughly 8-9 miles up-valley ... Swamp Creek Camp near mile 8.5, then leave the trail and bushwhack east into the upper Agnes Creek/Blue Basin drainage ... fording Agnes Creek or Spruce Creek') and the Swamp Creek Camp waypoint (distMi 8.1) should be removed, because they lead away from the peak; a researched line up Flat Creek or the West Fork Agnes Creek would have to replace them, and none is published. OpenStreetMap maps Rimrock Ridge as a ridge running from about 48.370 to 48.383 N and -121.018 to -120.969 W, and Swamp Creek Camp at 48.3097, -120.9205, so the ridge lies 4-5 miles north-west of that camp, not east of it; the trail pages already tried place it between upper Flat Creek and the West Fork Agnes Creek, whose trail leaves the PCT near Fivemile Camp. No 'Blue Basin' appears in the map data. No ascent account names a route, so a replacement approach would be invention, and removing the leg would leave the approach without a line; this needs a human with a map.

None states a car-to-car total for the Southwest Route, and summing legs would be a computed figure. No patch.

No second source for the East summit's one-way or round-trip distance, so dist_km, the summit waypoint and the 10 mi totalNote are not changed.

sectionBreakdown.note: Hike the long trail approach into the Stehekin backcountry, gaining much of the day's elevation on brushy, trailless ground before dropping a bit to a flat, water-adjacen…
Alpine start from camp with a light pack to tackle the cross-country ridge scramble to the 7,255 ft summit, then reverse the ascent line back to camp. Break camp and hike the full …

cleared_value.notes: From the Argonaut-Colchuck col (~7,700ft) gain the east ridge crest over low-angle blocks and broken granite steps, easing into the climb before the terrain steepens.
Surmount a compact, steeper granite tower via face moves and thin gear placements; this is the route's technical crux and the most sustained pitch on the ridge.
Weave over and around a series of towers along the crest, alternating short exposed steps with easier ledge traverses; belay from a horn where the ridge narrows.
Moderate climbing and scrambling up blocky granite toward the upper mountain, with route-finding between minor gendarmes rather than sustained difficulty.
Continue past another gendarme on the upper ridge, staying near the crest on exposed but moderate granite before the angle relents toward the summit spires.
Class 3-4 ridge traverse to the base of the summit block, finishing with a short nonexposed scramble past the block's small cave feature to the true summit.
First rappel down steep terrain toward the snow/talus below the notch, off a pre-placed sling on a rock.
Second rappel from a small tree, continuing down to the snow slopes; parties then traverse a snow-covered ledge toward the east gully.
